Although her language is perfect and she has more than enough knowledge to teach us, her evaluations about us are mostly poor. We are here to learn and make mistakes, instead of teaching us how to improve and fix those mistakes, she only points a finger at you and she does not try to direct you towards a better way. Her classes are usually fun and full of humour, yet this does not fulfill the expectations. There is a constant pressure while taking a course from her, even though she has so much wisdom to make us students better in our departments, we only leave with low grades and frustration with Valerie.

I find this unfortunate, but still I like her.

It is very difficult to fully understand what the lecturer expects from us. Her grading is quite low and her expectation is very high. I never find it right to just focus on grammar and reference errors to this degree and break notes just because we are making some grammar errors and reference errors. Nobody speaks and writes English perfectly. Even a British native speaker can make grammar mistakes, and we were expected to do so. The unexpected is losing a lot of points just because of this. I think the lecturer should retire now, she is very old and cannot remember some of the things she did or asked from us later when we told her. During this lesson, I am very nervous and cannot feel comfortable. I feel like the lecturer will be angry or a negative situation will occur at any moment. course: The course is quite comprehensive and understandable. There is not any problem.

I don't find group assignments absolutely useful or healthy. Supposedly we only take only one midterm and only one final exam, but we write tons of essays with group assignments and participation homework, and that costs two midterms already! Dealing with group homework every week is very stressful and adds even more burden to the student who already has many burdens. The requirement to use at least two texts and two secondary resources in the essays is never helpful at all; on the contrary, the student becomes puzzled and finds himself or herself in a deadlock. The syllabus should be reorganized, and I think the instructor must change the grading system as soon as possible. We are really working hard, and we are not getting the reward for our labor and pain. In this case, it causes the student's motivation to be severely broken and to feel lost from time to time and slowly get away from the course.

instructor: She is respectful and funny. I loved her personality she was aware of the hardness of learning through the screen. However, she loads you with a lot of work. You will have lots of readings to do and every week you will have a group meeting and discuss them and with respect you will write an essay. She asks every class whether you did the reading and took notes and grades you by your answer. But even though I sad "yes, yes" she graded me 70 something. And I find this question extremely unnecessary. What is the point, to grade participation? I believe there are better ways to grade participation like Moodle annotations etc. Also, in the beginning of the course she required everyone to turn their cameras and it was unnecessary and stressful. She then, said it wasn't necessary. She is humorous during the lecture which I liked. She is not generous with grading. She finds weird points that she breaks your grade like why you didn't mention the way the writer writes? But I will mention if I want to?? I am answering the essay question and the question doesn't ask what writers technique of writing means. She also breaks your points if you doesn't pay attention to punctuation. Excuse me this course is not a grammar course. She also expects you to send text to her regarding you met with your group every week. This is again, unnecessary in my opinion.
